objective: Same task-result quality at lower total cost. Fewer returned tokens is a mechanism, never the acceptance criterion.

arms.label: Agent without RepoContext
arms.description: The agent reads the repository with its own native tools. No repoctx index, instructions, MCP server, hook or session state is present.

arms.label: RepoContext 0.14.x integration
arms.description: repoctx init + index + integrate as shipped before this change: instructions, on-demand skill and MCP registration. No read-cost guard, no lifecycle-bound sessions.

arms.label: RepoContext integration plus read-cost guard and lifecycle sessions
arms.description: Arm 'current' plus 'repoctx integrate --guard', i.e. the opt-in read-cost guard and the context-epoch session binding added in 0.15.0.

fixed_across_arms: tool set available to the agent, apart from the arm's own setup

protocol.isolation: one fresh git worktree and one fresh agent context per run; no session, receipt or index state is carried between runs
protocol.order: counterbalanced: run index r uses arm order rotated by r, so arm position cannot correlate with repository or cache state

cache_modes.description: Fresh agent context, no provider prompt cache warm for this prompt prefix. Every run of a task/arm pair starts cold at repetition 1.

Immediately repeated prompt prefix within the provider's cache window, so repeated instruction and context tokens bill as cache reads. Measured and reported separately; never averaged into cold numbers.

protocol.retention: Failures, timeouts and retries stay in the denominator and in the cost total. Runs are never dropped for being unsuccessful or expensive.
protocol.holdout: Tasks flagged holdout=true are not inspected or tuned against before the release decision.
protocol.freeze: Tasks, acceptance checks and the rubric are frozen by the SHA-256 of this file. Changing any of them requires a new manifest id.

quality: acceptance: every acceptance check of the task passes
regressions: the repository's own test command passes after the change
defect_severity: none | minor | major | severe (rubric.md section 3)
spend: reasoning_tokens (only when the provider bills them separately from output)
billed_amount and billed_currency when the provider exposes them
usage_complete: false whenever any of the above was unavailable

accounting_rules: Billing categories are disjoint. Reasoning tokens are counted once; they are added only when the provider bills them outside the output category.
Report total spend and cost per accepted completion, where the denominator counts accepted completions and the numerator includes spend on failed and retried runs.
If no run of an arm is accepted, cost per accepted completion is undefined, never zero.
For flat subscriptions, estimated API-equivalent cost and quota consumption are reported separately from money actually billed.
Provider-reported usage is primary. Local tokenizer estimates and hypothetically avoided reads are reported as estimates, under their own labels, and never summed with billed figures.
Missing billing data makes a comparison incomplete. It never proves a saving.

promotion_criteria.no_evidence_loss: Frozen retrieval gates (docs/eval/holdout) unchanged, no new security or correctness regression in required task tests.
promotion_criteria.no_quality_loss: No lower observed acceptance or rubric quality, and no higher severe-defect or human-repair rate than arm 'current'.
promotion_criteria.cost: Lower measured total spend and lower cost per accepted completion than arm 'current'. Initial product target: at least 15 % lower cost per accepted completion. A target, not an achieved result.
promotion_criteria.uncertainty: Paired confidence intervals for quality and spend, including the largest quality regression still compatible with the data. Absence of a significant difference does not establish equal quality; inconclusive evidence keeps enforce mode experimental.
promotion_criteria.operations: Latency, per-task cost regressions and failure modes are reported explicitly. A policy is not enabled broadly if retries or friction erase its benefit.
